properties.name: Yellowstone National Park
properties.description: The world's first national park. Home to Old Faithful geyser and half of the planet's active geysers. Sits atop a supervolcano.

properties.name: Serengeti National Park
properties.description: Hosts the Great Migration — 1.5 million wildebeest and 250,000 zebra moving in an annual cycle. Setting of countless nature documentaries.

properties.name: Torres del Paine National Park
properties.description: Famous for its three granite towers, turquoise lakes, and the Grey Glacier. The W Trek is a bucket-list trekking route.

properties.name: Banff National Park
properties.description: Canada's first national park. Lake Louise's glacial-fed waters get their turquoise colour from rock flour suspended in the water.

properties.name: Kruger National Park
properties.description: One of Africa's largest game reserves. Home to the Big Five — lion, leopard, rhino, elephant, and buffalo.

properties.name: Fiordland National Park
properties.description: New Zealand's largest national park. Milford Sound was called the '8th wonder of the world' by Rudyard Kipling.

properties.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
properties.description: 16 terraced lakes connected by waterfalls, formed by mineral-rich water depositing travertine. Wooden boardwalks thread through the park.

properties.name: Jim Corbett National Park
properties.description: India's oldest national park and birthplace of Project Tiger. Named after hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett.

properties.name: Galápagos National Park
properties.description: Inspired Darwin's theory of evolution. Home to giant tortoises, marine iguanas, and blue-footed boobies — 97% of the archipelago is protected.

properties.name: Vatnajökull National Park
properties.description: Covers 14% of Iceland — Europe's largest glacier sits atop active volcanoes. Ice caves and subglacial eruptions make for a surreal landscape.
